newsitem.title: USA: Boeing, McDonnell Douglas to merge.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, McDonnell Douglas to merge.

text.p: Boeing and McDonnell Douglas will announce the merger of their two companies at a noon (1700 GMT) press conference on Sunday, sources said.
"It's going to to be the largest aerospace company in the world," a source familiar with the deal said.
The source gave no other details, but CNN reported the new company would have a worth of $40 billion.
The present chairman and chief executive officer of McDonnell Douglas, Harry Stonecipher, was expected to become the president and CEO of the new company, CNN said its sources told the network.
Phil Condit, the CEO of Boeing, was slated to become the chairman of the board of the new company, CNN said, according to its sources.
The two companies, Boeing specializing in commercial aircraft, and McDonnell Douglas, which specializes in military aircraft, have been known to be in merger discussions.
